<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Reported by the chainglass prime pij-lonely-antelope on 2026-11-02, measured against the live daemon; the prime re-measured `pij-rs --json state <seat>` at 1.32–1.33 s with the daemon otherwise idle (pid 67958, 10% CPU, 35 MB). The handler (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs, around state_card at :2860 and the held-delivery projection above it) reads registry, liveness, the latest card, the latest state record and held deliveries; at least one of those reads appears to scan the 4.16M-row spine per call. Asks: (1) one call fast, and concurrent calls not serialised; (2) a bulk read, all seats' cards in one call or the card fields on /v1/seats; (3) `stateNote`'s timestamp and cursor, like `statusAt`/`statusSeq`. Chainglass is another repo (read-only): ~/substrate/chainglass apps/web/src/features/089-first-class-pij/server/rs/start-pij-poller.ts and rs-client.ts. Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- One /v1/state call takes milliseconds, not seconds, whatever the spine size.
- Concurrent card reads don't queue behind each other.
- A client can read every seat's card in one call.
- The card says when its state note was written.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Deleting or compacting spine rows (that is a separate ruling).
- Changing chainglass.
- Changing the meaning of any existing card field.
